original_constraints: mandatory FIRST TOOL ACTION worker spawn before shell/editing
first runnable vertical slice plus early finite smoke and documentation as features land
MCP status at initial spawn and major stage boundaries including handoff
initial medium worker may produce bounded implementation proposal; later review needs concrete scope
current_constraints_observed: one cohesive bounded code/tests/examples/README slice then acceptance batch; split only for dependency or uncertainty
initial context-only reviewer/high alongside chief work, no first-tool serialization, no tools/files/polling/production code in initial pass
MCP optional chief decision support, at most two absent explicit stress protocol; no mandatory checkpoint or status-only turn
chief owns numerical/parsing/security/atomic boundaries and relevant malformed/empty/nonfinite/near-zero tests; helper evidence integrated once
instruction_comparison.comparison_limit: Only instruction source inspected; changed policy is not a new performance result.

findings.statement: Additional native attempts are not all child work: Ledger has 3 medium plus 3 additional xhigh; SafeZip has 6 medium plus 5 additional xhigh compared with A. Gateway counts are not agent counts.

B chief and child separately performed initial inventory/scope shell calls before first mutation. Ledger chief has 4 shell batches and child 2; SafeZip chief 5 and child 3. These overlap and are semantically related, not byte-identical duplicate commands.

Ledger has one genuinely standalone final MCP-only batch at 613.752 s. Its status at 473.101 s was batched with unittest, correcting an earlier completed-item-window inference. SafeZip all five MCP calls are batched with shell; reducing MCP call count alone cannot be equated with removing five full model turns.

SafeZip invokes one explicit helper follow-up at 641.033 s, causing the same child to inspect again at 645.624 s. Its six medium requests span two phases. This is a real extra review phase, but its usefulness or necessity cannot be decided from metadata alone.

SafeZip has an exact repeated test command at 584.391 and 614.158 s; a test patch intervenes, so waste is not proven. Other similarly classified inventory/smoke/test batches have different command hashes or changing code.

All 77 requests in these four arms completed semantically, with no transport failure; network cause is not implicated by these records. Cached input varies substantially, so extra input is not equal to extra paid or subscription cost.

proposals.change: For bounded CLI tasks, consolidate one necessary task/rules inventory, then implement code, required tests, examples and README as one coherent slice before a finite acceptance batch. Keep substantive security and atomic boundary checks.

Use one supplied-context reviewer/high in parallel with chief work; no helper initial directory probing or serialized first-tool barrier. Return bounded acceptance risks, integrate once; follow up only for an observed unresolved defect.
proposals.risk: high effort can itself take longer; one changed-policy preregistered test required

proposals.change: Make chief status optional and batched, maximum two absent an explicit protocol. Remove post-acceptance/final status-only turn. Do not attribute full inference latency to the measured subsecond MCP call itself.

Batch independent finite smoke/help/examples/tests after the coherent implementation. Re-run after meaningful source/test changes or unresolved failures; keep real control/atomic/security tests, not an arbitrary minimum-check reduction.

Retain per-profile request/usage/cache and interval union, plus phase-aware shell classifications. Treat shell/child overlaps, provider scheduling, token generation and caching as separate unknown contributors; require both normal completion and unchanged acceptance for a speed claim.

limitations: No hidden grader cases, application source, reasoning text, raw commands or request bodies are included or inspected as standalone source. Rollout argument text is classified locally, never executed.

Literal command classification can overmatch embedded fixture code; it is an indicator, not a proof that every tagged operation executed. Patch metadata records paths by class only, never application code.
Open/body-read timings include provider/transport/generation effects; they are not TTFT, isolated transport wait or model-compute time. Concurrent durations must not be added to elapsed time.
Native time outside request interval union includes startup, shell tools, serialization and uninstrumented gaps; it is not all avoidable orchestration overhead.
Usage sums use individual gateway/native records, not cumulative token budgets. Unknown API cost/quota remains null. Unattributed xhigh requests have no invented cause.

One observed pair per task with different implementations cannot establish a causal policy contribution, universal acceleration, or a model-quality explanation. No new performance claim follows from current instruction changes.
A own-cwd persisted rollout was absent. Exact-cwd lookup was not widened. Shared native state limits strict isolation claims.

method.request_interval_basis: native event elapsed-at-completion minus per-request duration; union retains actual overlap, rounded to milliseconds
method.own_session_binding: Exact two cwd spellings only; SHA256(thread id) must match root/child metadata, child source parent link must match root; raw identities and global rollout paths withheld
method.native_vs_gateway_accounting: Individual native token records match gateway usage tuples exactly; unmatched gateway records remain unattributed
method.command_classification: Literal cmd strings and patch path class metadata only; never execute rollout text; same native batch may contain multiple tools
read_only_checks: all 77 requests completed and semantically terminal
aggregate sums match gateway metrics for all four arms
every available native per-request usage tuple uniquely matches a gateway record
all file inputs and exact owned rollouts SHA256-stable during read
method.output_safety: Only task-relative evidence paths, hashes, fixed classifications, counts and numeric timings; no raw prompts, commands, response bodies, identities, auth or grader data
